verdict_text: NO. The merge uses `tmp = b + λ(f1 − b)` and then `tmp + λ(f2 − tmp)`, so the second task vector is taken against the already-modified base rather than the unmodified base, violating Required result step 2 (`out[X] = base[X] + λ(ft1[X] − base[X]) + λ(ft2[X] − base[X])`). This is exactly the ordering hazard the specification warns about, and the resulting deviation is `λ²(f1 − b)`, which is not absorbed by the 1e-3 relative Frobenius tolerance in general. Everything else (shared-tensor verification before any modification, merged count of 64, output count of 244, float32 computation with cast back to float16, unchanged tensors copied from base) conforms.
expected_defect: Task vector 2 is computed against the base after task vector 1 has already been added, so the second delta is taken from the wrong reference point.
